title: minimap hover probe and screen-reader announced metrics for long-series charts
creator: Alex Chen
description: Add a compact minimap (overview) with an interactive hover probe that surfaces contextual metrics for the visible window and provides concise screen-reader announcements summarizing the current viewport. Goal is to make exploration of long time-series faster and screen-reader friendly while keeping DOM and CPU overhead low.
background: Current time-series components are hard to navigate for long signals. Keyboard and screen-reader users get only the last focused datapoint via existing tooltip semantics; teams building observability dashboards requested both a glanceable overview and a narrated summary of the visible window. Engineering has reported jank in large-series tooltips due to per-point DOM bindings and full-series accessibility nodes.
user_stories: As a power user I want a small overview so I can jump to interesting ranges without zooming repeatedly
As a keyboard or screen-reader user I want a short summary (min, max, median, trend) of the currently visible window so I can understand the section without interacting with many points
As an engineer I want the solution to avoid per-point DOM growth so charts remain performant on 100k+ points
constraints: Must work with canvas rendering fallback and DOM SVG hybrid modes
Announcements must be <= 300 characters to avoid verbose SR output
Implementation should not add O(n) DOM elements per series for large datasets
Feature must respect existing WCAG patterns and Redwood Console keyboard shortcuts
proposed_solution: Introduce a thin minimap strip below the main chart showing an overview rasterized thumbnail of the full series (canvas-only representation).

Add a hover probe tied to the minimap: mouse hover or keyboard focus over the minimap moves the main viewport center and shows an ephemeral probe card with context metrics for the highlighted window (avg, min, max, percentile, slope).
Expose a screen-reader only live region that emits short, structured announcements when the viewport changes: e.g., 'Showing 12:00–14:00 UTC, avg 72.4, max 123, rising'.
Keyboard interactions: tab into minimap, arrow keys move the window in fixed steps, shift+arrows resize window, Enter toggles a pinned probe card that remains visible until dismissed.
Performance: compute window aggregates in a webworker for large series; use memoized decimation to render minimap thumbnail. Reuse existing runtime batching APIs for updates to avoid layout thrash.
accessibility_considerations: Use aria-live polite or assertive depending on context; default to polite unless user explicitly requests immediate updates
Provide a concise aria-label for the minimap control, and an aria-describedby that links to the live summary region
Ensure pinned probe card is keyboard-focusable and announced as a dialog-like region with role=region and aria-label
Offer a user preference to silence automatic SR announcements (for users who prefer manual exploration)
performance_plan: Benchmark: add config in perf harness to test charts at 10k, 100k, 1M points with minimap enabled and disabled
Measure main-thread time for viewport pan events and SR announcement generation; target additional main-thread overhead < 12ms per interaction for 100k points
Implement progressive fallbacks: if total_points > 250k, switch minimap to precomputed thumbnail and restrict probe metrics to percentiles rather than full stats
Run memory allocation checks to ensure no per-point DOM nodes created by this feature
acceptance_criteria: Minimap renders below chart in canvas and hybrid modes and visually matches design spec (Figma link).
Hover probe surfaces within 100ms of hover and shows the expected metrics for the highlighted window.
Screen-reader announces a concise summary when viewport changes, and announcements are configurable in user preferences.
No visible jank for datasets up to 100k points in Chrome on MacBook Pro baseline (tracked in perf dashboard).
Design review and accessibility review approvals recorded in this ticket comments with next steps assigned to engineering.
rollout_plan: Beta rollout to 10% of production users for two weeks with perf telemetry collection
Collect qualitative feedback from UX research sessions before full launch
GA in console-2025.03 once perf and a11y signoff complete
